concepts.name: Primary Market: Definition, Function and Capital Formation Role
key_dimensions: Primary market as the source of fresh capital — distinction from mere transfer of ownership
Direct link to GDP growth and productive investment vs secondary market's liquidity function
Why primary market activity is a leading indicator of economic confidence
UPSC trap: Primary market transactions increase money supply in corporate sector; secondary market does NOT

concepts.name: Initial Public Offering (IPO): Mechanism and Regulatory Framework
key_dimensions: Fixed Price vs Book Building method — price discovery differences and SEBI mandate
SEBI ICDR (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations governing IPOs
Role of BRLM (Book Running Lead Manager), registrars, and underwriters
UPSC trap: IPO is primary market; listing on exchange post-IPO shifts to secondary market

concepts.name: Book Building Process: Price Discovery Mechanism
key_dimensions: Price band, floor price, cut-off price — definitions and investor category applicability
QIB, HNI, and Retail investor allocation percentages under SEBI norms (75:15:10 ratio)
Green Shoe Option (over-allotment option) — price stabilization post-listing
UPSC trap: Book building is price discovery; fixed price method has no price discovery

concepts.name: Follow-on Public Offer (FPO) vs Rights Issue vs Bonus Issue
key_dimensions: FPO: Fresh shares to public at large vs Rights Issue: proportional offer to existing shareholders
Bonus Issue: capitalization of reserves — no fresh capital inflow (UPSC trap: not a primary market instrument in true sense)
Dilution of EPS and promoter shareholding implications in FPO vs Rights Issue
SEBI eligibility criteria differences for FPO vs Rights Issue (fast-track rights issue route)

concepts.name: Private Placement, QIP and Preferential Allotment: Alternate Primary Market Routes
key_dimensions: Private Placement vs Public Issue — investor number threshold (SEBI: >200 persons = public issue)
Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP): listed companies raising capital from QIBs without prospectus
Preferential Allotment: shares to select investors — SEBI pricing formula (VWAP-based floor price)
UPSC trap: QIP bypasses prospectus requirement but is still a primary market activity

concepts.name: Secondary Market: Stock Exchanges — BSE and NSE Architecture
key_dimensions: BSE (1875) — oldest in Asia; NSE introduced screen-based electronic trading in 1994
Demutualisation of stock exchanges — separation of ownership, management, and trading rights
SEBI recognition criteria for stock exchanges under Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956
UPSC trap: Secondary market does NOT provide capital to companies — only liquidity to investors

concepts.name: SEBI: Regulatory Jurisdiction over Primary and Secondary Markets
key_dimensions: SEBI Act 1992 — triple mandate: protect investors, develop markets, regulate markets
SEBI's jurisdiction over primary market (prospectus vetting, disclosure) vs secondary market (trading surveillance, manipulation)
Quasi-legislative, quasi-judicial, and executive powers of SEBI
UPSC trap: RBI regulates government securities market (G-Sec) — NOT SEBI; overlap area frequently tested

concepts.name: Depositories and Dematerialization: NSDL and CDSL
key_dimensions: Depository vs Depository Participant (DP) — two-tier structure under Depositories Act, 1996
NSDL (promoted by NSE, IDBI, UTI) vs CDSL (promoted by BSE) — functional comparison
Dematerialization eliminating physical share certificates — reduction of settlement risk
UPSC trap: Depositories are part of secondary market infrastructure but also record primary allotments

concepts.name: Clearing and Settlement System: T+1 Rolling Settlement
key_dimensions: Evolution: T+5 → T+3 → T+2 → T+1 settlement cycle in India (India among first globally for T+1)
Role of Clearing Corporations: NSCCL (NSE) and ICCL (BSE) as central counterparties
DVP (Delivery vs Payment) mechanism eliminating principal risk
UPSC trap: T+1 reduces counterparty risk and systemic risk — NOT the same as real-time settlement (T+0 is different)

concepts.name: Market Capitalization: Types and Significance as Economic Indicator
key_dimensions: Large-cap, Mid-cap, Small-cap classification by SEBI (top 100, 101-250, beyond 250 by full market cap)
Market cap-to-GDP ratio (Buffett Indicator) — measuring market overvaluation/undervaluation
Free-float market capitalization vs full market capitalization — index construction relevance
UPSC trap: Sensex is based on free-float market cap of 30 companies; Nifty 50 also free-float based

concepts.name: Stock Market Indices: Sensex and Nifty — Construction and Significance
key_dimensions: Sensex: BSE, base year 1978-79, base value 100; Nifty 50: NSE, base year 1995, base value 1000
Index as barometer of market sentiment and leading macroeconomic indicator
Sectoral indices (Nifty Bank, Nifty IT) vs broad market indices — different policy signals
UPSC trap: Fall in index does NOT mean all stocks fell — weighted average effect; index composition matters

concepts.name: Prospectus and DRHP: Disclosure Obligations in Primary Market
key_dimensions: Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) filed with SEBI; Red Herring Prospectus lacks final price; Final Prospectus has all details
Material disclosures: risk factors, use of proceeds, promoter background — investor protection rationale
SEBI's 'Observe' letter vs 'No objection' — SEBI does not guarantee issue quality (UPSC trap)
Shelf Prospectus: allows multiple tranches without fresh prospectus (used by banks, financial institutions)

concepts.name: Investor Categories in Capital Markets: QIB, HNI, Retail
key_dimensions: QIB: FIIs, mutual funds, insurance companies, scheduled commercial banks — SEBI defined
Retail Individual Investor (RII): application up to ₹2 lakh; HNI/NII: above ₹2 lakh
Anchor Investor concept: QIB subset allotted shares before IPO opens — price signaling role
UPSC trap: Anchor investors have a 30-day lock-in; retail investors have no lock-in post-listing

concepts.name: Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI) in Capital Markets: Primary vs Secondary Market Routes
key_dimensions: FPI can invest in both primary (IPO/FPO) and secondary markets — SEBI FPI Regulations 2019
FPI investment limits: sectoral caps, aggregate limit linked to paid-up capital
Distinction: FPI (secondary market, portfolio) vs FDI (primary market, direct ownership control)
UPSC trap: FII was replaced by FPI in 2014; FPI capital flow is 'hot money' — exchange rate and CAD implications

concepts.name: Debt Market: Primary Issuance vs Secondary Trading of Bonds
key_dimensions: Government Securities (G-Secs): primary issuance via RBI auctions (not SEBI) — uniform price vs multiple price auction
Corporate bonds: primary issuance via private placement (dominant) or public issue; secondary trading on BSE/NSE
Credit rating mandatory for public issue of debt — SEBI registered CRAs (CRISIL, ICRA, CARE, India Ratings)
UPSC trap: G-Sec market regulated by RBI under FRBM; corporate bond market under SEBI — dual regulatory landscape

concepts.name: Derivatives Market: Relationship with and Distinction from Primary/Secondary Markets
key_dimensions: Derivatives (futures, options) are secondary market instruments — no capital raised for companies
Derivatives derive value from underlying (equity, commodity, currency, index) — not a primary market activity
SEBI regulates equity and index derivatives; RBI regulates currency derivatives; SEBI regulates commodity derivatives (post-2015 FMC merger)
UPSC trap: Derivatives market is part of capital market ecosystem but does NOT mobilize savings into investment directly

concepts.name: Market Intermediaries: Brokers, Sub-brokers, Investment Bankers — Registration and Role
key_dimensions: SEBI mandatory registration for brokers, merchant bankers, portfolio managers, investment advisers
Merchant banker (Category I only retained by SEBI) — manages primary market issues
Stockbroker operates only in secondary market; Investment banker operates in primary market — UPSC confusion area
SEBI's grievance redressal: SCORES platform and ODR (Online Dispute Resolution) portal

concepts.name: SME IPO and Emerge/SME Platform: Relaxed Listing Norms
key_dimensions: BSE SME and NSE Emerge platforms — separate listing framework for Small and Medium Enterprises
Relaxed eligibility: lower post-issue capital requirement vs main board IPO norms
Market maker mandatory for SME IPOs — liquidity provision mechanism (absent in main board)
UPSC trap: SME IPO is still a primary market activity; migration from SME to main board is possible upon meeting criteria

concepts.name: ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount): Primary Market Payment Reform
key_dimensions: ASBA: funds blocked in investor's bank account — not transferred until allotment; interest earned during blocking period
Mandatory for all IPO applicants since 2016 — replaced cheque-based applications
Self Certified Syndicate Banks (SCSBs) designated by SEBI to offer ASBA facility
UPSC trap: UPI-based ASBA for retail investors (up to ₹5 lakh) — linkage with payment system modernization

concepts.name: Stock Exchange Circuit Breakers and Market-Wide Risk Management
key_dimensions: Index-based market-wide circuit breakers: 10%, 15%, 20% triggers — halt duration varies by time of day
Individual scrip price bands: 2%, 5%, 10%, 20% — differs from index-level circuit breakers
Upper Circuit/Lower Circuit — asymmetry trap: hitting lower circuit does not mean trading stops for buyers
UPSC relevance: Circuit breakers as systemic risk containment tool — linked to financial stability mandate of SEBI
